To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
driving cycle optimized interior permanent magnet synchronous machines show a significantly better performance in terms of loss energy over driving cycles.
the loss energy of a permanent magnet synchronous machine is significantly reduced when the design is optimized for the driving cycle instead of being optimized against the rated point.
the design optimization based on a driving cycle leads to significant loss reductions and that the loss savings depend on the machine length.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of a design optimization method for interior permanent magnet synchronous machines based on the ARTEMIS urban driving cycle.

the design optimization of synchronous machines with respect to the loss energy over driving cycles, and the results can be used for a more realistic design process of synchronous machines for electric vehicle applications.
the development of an optimized design of synchronous machines based on driving cycles, which is an essential step towards the design of highly efficient electric vehicle drives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cycle-based optimization is a very promising approach to reduce the loss energy in electric vehicle applications.
driving cycle-based design optimizations are highly recommended.
a design optimization of electric machines based on the rated point loss is not suitable for applications with a high number of operating points.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the driving cycle optimization is more efficient than the rated point optimization.
the ARTEMIS optimized machines are more suitable for electric vehicle applications than rated point optimized machines.
a driving cycle-based optimization is essential for the design of permanent magnet machines for electric vehicle applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design optimization of synchronous machines should be based on the driving cycle to be used, as the driving cycle has a significant influence on the loss distribution and thus the machine design.
driving cycle based design optimization is a very promising approach for electric drive design and should be considered in future work.

the design optimization against the loss energy over the driving cycle is a more suitable approach for synchronous machines with buried magnets in comparison to the design against the rated point losses.
